prompt: Two identical wires X and Y each contain a row of evenly spaced positive charges when no current flows. Equal currents (conventional current = flow of positive charge) then flow in the two wires, but in opposite directions. In the frame of reference of a positive charge moving with the current in wire Y, how do the positive-charge distributions in the two wires appear?
options: Wire X's positive charges appear more closely spaced (X appears positively charged); wire Y's positive charges appear at their normal spacing
Both wires' positive charges appear at their normal spacing
Wire Y's positive charges appear more closely spaced; wire X's appear more widely spaced
Both wires' positive charges appear more closely spaced by the same amount
answer: Wire X's positive charges appear more closely spaced (X appears positively charged); wire Y's positive charges appear at their normal spacing
